monthly_review.summary: This month shows a clear shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic base work — evidenced by increased Z1/Z2 time and reduced HR and pace intensity — though total volume and session frequency have declined significantly compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 rose from 55% to 82% of total HR time, while Z4+Z5 dropped from 19% to 2%, indicating a deliberate (but possibly overcorrected) move away from threshold and VO2-max stimulus.

goal_tracker.message: You need 9.3 more km across 3 additional sessions in the remaining 16 days to match last month’s 38.0 km — averaging ~3.1 km per session. Given your recent 2.5–9.5 km runs, adding three 3–4 km Zone 2 runs is highly achievable.

insights.title: Slight efficiency erosion despite lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.66 to 13.43 m/beat while avg HR dropped 7 bpm — suggesting less effective oxygen utilization per heartbeat, possibly due to reduced neuromuscular coordination or pacing inconsistency across varied efforts.

insights.title: Near-total absence of high-intensity stimulus
insights.body: Z4 and Z5 accounted for only 2% of this month’s HR time (vs. 19% last month), with zero Z5 effort recorded — meaning no VO2-max or race-pace running occurred in May so far, risking aerobic power deconditioning.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff emerging at faster paces
insights.body: On 2026-05-16 (7:27/min/km, HR 148), stride length jumped to 94.35 cm (+24.6 cm vs. 5/6 long run) while ground contact dropped to 286 ms — indicating compensatory overstriding under fatigue, likely reducing efficiency and increasing injury risk.

insights.title: Low cumulative load despite moderate TE on key runs
insights.body: Although the 5/16 run delivered 3.2 aerobic TE (highest this month), it followed just one 2.5 km run 3 days prior — insufficient recovery sequencing to sustain that stimulus, and overall monthly training load (as reflected in total km and sessions) is down 23% vs April.

recommendations.action: Perform a 4.0 km Zone 2 run (HR 125–135 bpm) within next 48 hours, focusing on maintaining cadence ≥146 spm and stride length ≤72 cm (use real-time cadence/stride alerts on Garmin).
recommendations.reason: Your recent cadence peaked at 150 spm but stride length ballooned to 94.35 cm under fatigue; re-establishing neuromuscular control at sustainable intensities will protect efficiency and reduce impact stress.

recommendations.action: Insert one 6-minute progressive surge at end of next Zone 2 run: increase pace from 10:30 to 8:45 min/km (447 sec/km — your best pace) over 3 intervals of 2 min each, with 90 sec jog recovery between.
recommendations.reason: Your best recorded pace (447 sec/km) occurred in April, and Z4/Z5 time has vanished — this safely reintroduces lactate-buffering stimulus without requiring full interval sessions.

recommendations.action: After your next run >5 km, review Garmin’s 'Recovery Time' and 'HRV Status' metrics — if either shows 'Limited Recovery' or 'Below Baseline', skip the following scheduled run and substitute with 30 min Zone 1 walking (HR <115 bpm).
recommendations.reason: Your 5/16 run (HR 148, TE 3.2) was preceded by only light activity, yet vertical oscillation rose to 8.1 cm (vs. 7.1–7.7 in prior runs) — an early sign of compromised fatigue resilience.

weekly_focus.description: Rebuild sustainable endurance capacity while reinforcing efficient movement patterns under fatigue — prioritizing consistency of cadence, controlled stride length, and timely recovery signals over raw volume or pace.
suggested_sessions: 4 km Zone 2 run (HR 125–135 bpm) with cadence ≥146 spm focus
6 km mixed-effort run: 3 km Zone 2 + 3 × (2 min progressive surge @ 447 sec/km + 90 sec jog)
30 min Zone 1 walk (HR <115 bpm) with post-session HRV check
